Yes,
B. Braun
sells and distributes medical devices
, but they do not focus on consumer-grade or patient-worn "wearable" health monitors (like smartwatches or continuous glucose patches). Instead, their portfolio centers on clinical and hospital-based technology
MarketsandMarkets

B. Braun does not make consumer smartwatches, wearable ECGs, sleep trackers, or personal continuous glucose monitors (CGMs)
. Instead,
B. Braun
is a global medical technology company that focuses on hospital-grade clinical devices, such as
smart infusion pumps
, dialysis systems, and clinical remote data management rather than consumer-wearable health trackers.
B. Braun
B. Braun Blood Glucose Products
Omnitest Series:
B. Braun previously manufactured standard, spot-check blood glucose meters like the
Omnitest 3
and
Omnitest 5
for capillary blood testing. These require finger-prick test strips rather than continuous interstitial monitoring.
Clinical Glucose Monitoring:
They research specialized intravascular/arterial sensors (like the
SGC Plus
) intended for glycemic control in critical ICU hospital settings, not personal daily wear.

Consumer Wearables & Remote Monitoring Alternatives
Continuous Glucose Monitors (CGMs):
Real-time consumer and patient-owned CGMs are made by companies like Abbott (
FreeStyle Libre
) and Dexcom (

Smartwatches & Wearable ECG:
Brands like Apple, Samsung, and Garmin manufacture consumer smartwatches with on-demand ECG and pulse-tracking capabilities.

Remote Patient Monitoring (RPM):
Dedicated home and telehealth remote monitoring platforms utilize cellular-enabled blood pressure cuffs, pulse oximeters, and weight scales integrated into clinical software ecosystems.
